ads_ratio.reason: Equinox is a direct-listed foreign private issuer: one NYSE American-traded EQX share is one common share, so no ADS conversion applies; per-share figures and the traded price are on the same basis.
ads_ratio.source: Form 40-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025: the securities registered under Section 12(b) are the company's common shares, trading symbol EQX, listed directly on the NYSE American (and on the TSX under the same symbol) — the NYSE American security is the common share itself, not an ADS; company disclosure in its own releases states 'Equinox Gold's common shares are listed on the TSX and the NYSE American under the trading symbol EQX'

moat_against: Pure commodity price taker — no pricing power; earnings are a leveraged function of the gold price
ROIC proxy never above ~7% in FY2019-FY2025 and near zero in FY2022-23 (fundamentals.json) — no evidence of returns above the cost of capital through a cycle
High cost position: consolidated AISC $1,959/oz in Q2 2025 (search-cited)
Reserves deplete every year and must be replaced with heavy capex — FY2025 capex was $692.3M against $818.3M of OCF
Serial dilution: diluted share count compounding at 27.5%/yr (engine), driven by equity-financed acquisitions (Calibre closed June 17, 2025)
moat_for: Scale: 663,921 oz produced in 2025, guided 700,000-800,000 oz for 2026 (search-cited company presentation)
Two long-life Canadian cornerstone mines (Greenstone, Valentine) now ramping
Americas-only jurisdictions (Canada, USA, Brazil, Nicaragua) — no single-country concentration at the asset level
moat_justification: A gold miner is a pure price taker on a depleting asset — no pricing power, no switching costs, no network effects. Equinox sits on the weak end even for the sector: the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json runs 7.3% / 5.4% / 4.1% / 0.3% / 1.2% / 2.7% / 4.9% for FY2019-FY2025 — never sustained above a plausible cost of capital in any year — and consolidated AISC was $1,959/oz in Q2 2025 (search-cited), high for a senior producer. What keeps it off 0-1 is real scale and asset life: two long-life Canadian cornerstone mines (Greenstone, Valentine) ramping, an Americas-only portfolio, and production of 663,921 oz in 2025 (search-cited company presentation). Against: reserves deplete and must be rebought with capex, the share count has compounded at 27.5%/yr (engine) on acquisition equity, and execution has repeatedly lagged guidance at the flagship mines.
name: Equinox Gold Corp.
one_liner: Price-taking gold miner with a weak cost position and a serial-dilution record, moat 2/10 — Tier F: no positive normalized owner's earnings (3-yr median OE/share is -$0.10; OE positive in only 1 of the last 5 fiscal years), so the OE DCF produces no IV and no price clears a 15% hurdle on normalized numbers; the $11.15 price is a bet on the current gold price and the Greenstone/Valentine ramp, not on through-cycle earnings power.
